# AMD Instinct hardware access and vLLM ROCm serving validation campaign

## Description

Resolves the strategy's gating unknown for serving: whether vLLM serving on AMD
ROCm reaches functional and performance parity with the productized CUDA builds
for the supported model set. The epic first secures access to dedicated AMD
Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access, which the strategy leaves
unresolved — then executes the validation campaign and produces the parity data
and the go/no-go scope that defines which models are cleared for productization.

## Scope

- Resolve hardware access: evaluate procurement versus partner-lab options for
  dedicated AMD Instinct nodes and secure access, documenting the chosen path,
  node specifications, and the availability window.
- Stand up the validation environment on the secured nodes: AMD GPU driver and
  device-plugin prerequisites, and the platform serving stack running vLLM ROCm
  images from currently published upstream ROCm builds.
- Define the validation plan before execution: the supported model set,
  functional pass/fail criteria against the CUDA baseline, and performance
  parity thresholds.
- Execute functional validation: for each model in the supported model set, run
  vLLM serving on ROCm and verify functional correctness against the CUDA
  baseline.
- Execute performance validation: measure serving throughput and latency per
  model on ROCm versus the CUDA baseline and record the parity assessment.
- Produce the go/no-go report: per-model functional and performance results, the
  list of models cleared for productization, and any systemic ROCm findings
  relevant to the PyTorch training plans.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Dedicated AMD Instinct nodes are available to the validation effort via
  procurement or partner-lab access, with the chosen access path, node
  specifications, and availability window documented (resolves the strategy's
  hardware-access open question).
- The validation plan is defined and frozen before campaign execution,
  enumerating the supported model set, functional pass/fail criteria, and
  performance parity thresholds.
- Functional results exist for every model in the supported model set, each
  marked pass or fail against the CUDA baseline.
- Performance measurements with a parity assessment against the CUDA baseline
  exist for every model in the supported model set.
- A go/no-go report defines the model set cleared for productization and flags
  any systemic ROCm issues that would affect PyTorch training support.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): a validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
  establishing functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
  supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization.

# vLLM ROCm serving runtime productization

## Description

Productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models the validation
campaign clears, mirroring the existing CUDA runtime productization: image
builds in the existing midstream runtime repository, ServingRuntime templates,
and a support statement. KServe requires no code changes for this enablement —
the ROCm runtime runs under the existing InferenceService machinery — so KServe
compatibility is validated as part of this epic rather than changed.

## Scope

- Build and release the vLLM ROCm runtime image variant in the existing
  midstream runtime repository, pinned to an upstream ROCm release aligned with
  the target release train. Upstream ROCm image cadence is controlled by AMD
  and the upstream communities; if releases do not align with the release
  train, apply and document a mitigation such as a self-maintained build.
- Define the ServingRuntime / ClusterServingRuntime templates that expose the
  ROCm variant for the cleared models, requesting AMD GPU resources
  (amd.com/gpu).
- Validate KServe InferenceServices using the ROCm runtime on AMD Instinct
  nodes, in the deployment modes the platform supports for GPU serving.
- Document supportability boundaries: the supported model list (the
  campaign-cleared set), driver prerequisites, and known limitations.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The vLLM ROCm runtime image builds and releases through the existing runtime
  build pipeline.
- ServingRuntime templates for the ROCm variant deploy InferenceServices that
  serve every model on the campaign-cleared list on AMD Instinct nodes.
- KServe InferenceService lifecycle (deployment and endpoint readiness) works
  with the ROCm runtime without KServe code changes — passive-component
  validation for KServe.
- The shipped image is based on an upstream ROCm release aligned with the
  target release train, or a documented mitigation for misalignment exists.
- The supported model list in the support statement matches the campaign-cleared
  set; models not cleared are excluded and noted.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime productized for the models
  the validation campaign clears.
- Carries the passive-component validation for KServe (no code changes; same
  owning team as the serving runtime).

# PyTorch ROCm training support

## Description

Makes PyTorch training on ROCm a supported path for single- and multi-GPU jobs
admitted through Kueue: PyTorchJobs running PyTorch ROCm builds on AMD Instinct
nodes, covering both single-GPU and multi-worker topologies.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob workers to run PyTorch ROCm images on AMD GPU nodes for
  single-GPU and multi-GPU (multi-worker) training topologies.
- Validate multi-worker jobs with gang semantics admitted through Kueue on AMD
  nodes.
- Make any Training Operator changes required for AMD GPU resource handling —
  expected to be minimal, since the operator is accelerator-agnostic; changes
  are limited to what validation surfaces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A single-GPU PyTorchJob using a PyTorch ROCm image completes a training run
  successfully on an AMD Instinct node.
- A multi-GPU (multi-worker) PyTorchJob completes on AMD Instinct nodes with
  all workers scheduled on AMD GPU nodes.
- Multi-worker jobs are admitted through Kueue with amd.com/gpu quota
  accounting, with all-or-nothing gang semantics preserved (the quota and
  admission behavior is supplied by the parallel queueing-and-quota work, whose
  acceptance criteria cover these same job shapes).
- Training behavior on ROCm is functionally correct against the CUDA baseline
  for a representative training workload.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs
  admitted through Kueue — training-operator portion.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling

## Description

Extends the platform's queueing and quota layer to handle AMD GPU resources:
ClusterQueue resource flavors for amd.com/gpu, quota accounting, and
all-or-nothing admission for jobs requesting AMD GPUs, mirroring the established
NVIDIA GPU quota pattern.

## Scope

- Define and validate ClusterQueue resource flavors covering amd.com/gpu for
  AMD GPU node pools.
- Validate quota accounting and all-or-nothing (gang) admission for jobs
  requesting amd.com/gpu, for the single-GPU and multi-GPU (multi-worker)
  training job shapes that the PyTorch ROCm training support validates against.
- Make any Kueue changes required for AMD GPU resource handling — expected to be
  configuration-level; code changes only if validation surfaces gaps.
- Document the recommended quota configuration for AMD GPU pools for inclusion
  in platform documentation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- ClusterQueue quota accounting correctly tracks amd.com/gpu requests and usage
  on AMD GPU nodes.
- A single-GPU job requesting amd.com/gpu is admitted under quota enforcement
  and runs to completion.
- A multi-GPU (multi-worker) job requesting amd.com/gpu is admitted with
  all-or-nothing gang semantics — either all workers are placed on AMD GPU
  nodes or the job stays queued.
- Quota behavior for amd.com/gpu is equivalent to the established NVIDIA GPU
  (nvidia.com/gpu) quota behavior for the same job shapes.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): PyTorch training on ROCm supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs
  admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling — queueing-and-quota
  portion.
